A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CodeQuant study. All 19 pages, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A.1-A.7, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original accuracy, perplexity, ablation and GPU simulation results in Section 4, plus CPU measurements and additional analyses in Appendices A.4-A.7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and simulation results, including Tables 1-11 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: The AOS rotations, POG permutation, ACCF centroid optimization with router KL regularization, and LUT kernel procedure are unchanged, including the architecture-specific appendix details.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WikiText2/C4 language-modeling, ARC/HellaSwag/MMLU/PIQA/WinoGrande QA, and GSM8K/MATH500 reasoning evaluations. GPU and CPU test scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding experiments, including RTN, SmoothQuant, SqueezeLLM and QuaRot in Tables 1 and 7; DuQuant and SpinQuant with Hadamard transforms in Tables 2 and 8; and Llama.cpp baselines in Table 9.

E3.justification: Calibration sample counts and iterations, bitwidths, group sizes, prompting settings, metrics, GPU simulation configuration and CPU testing procedures are identical. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The AOS, KL-penalty and bitwidth ablations in Tables 4-6, and the POG and router-stability analyses in Tables 10-11, test the same questions with unchanged evidence.

E5.justification: Both retain the same fixed-random-seed statement and statistical reporting practices. Neither adds repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1-11 and Figure 5 are unchanged, including appendix accuracy, CPU latency and memory, POG, and router-stability results. Reported rankings and qualitative findings are also identical.

T1.justification: Equations 1-10, the optimization derivations, rotation and permutation invariance arguments, and Appendix A.2's mathematical analysis are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about unified clustering and quantization, accuracy-efficiency advantages, and speedups of up to 4.15 times.

C2.justification: Interpretations of POG applicability, KL-based routing preservation and CPU/GPU performance are identical. Section 3.4 retains the same qualification that a full hardware implementation is beyond scope.

D1.justification: Implementation details, calibration hyperparameters, preprocessing times, hardware and simulator settings, appendix pseudocode, and code-access statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works and positioning relative to prior quantization, clustering and LUT methods are identical.

P1.justification: On page 7, v2 corrects 'Section ??' to 'Section 4.3' when referring to latency evaluation. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The updated arXiv stamp is repositioned in the first-page margin. Figures 1-5, Tables 1-11, Algorithm 1 and the main-text and appendix page organization retain their layouts.

improvement.justification: v2 repairs one broken cross-reference and updates the arXiv stamp. This slightly improves navigation to existing latency evidence, but the methods, results, explanations, reproducibility information and appendices are unchanged. The edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
